title: The kings and queens of England.
lede: Every monarch from William the Conqueror to Charles III, nearly a thousand years of them, in order: when they reigned, which house they belonged to, and who came next. With the old rhyme, a timeline drawn to scale, and a hook for each.

card.title: Kings and queens
card.desc: William I to Charles III in order: reigns, houses and successors, with the rhyme and a timeline to scale.

map.label: name
map.hint: Each bar is as long as the reign. Point at one to see who it was; they fill in as I master them.

groups.label: Normans
groups.note: 1066–1154: the Conqueror, his sons, and a nephew who started a civil war.

groups.label: Plantagenets
groups.note: 1154–1399: Lionheart, Magna Carta, and a run of Edwards.

groups.label: York
groups.note: 1461–1485: the white rose, the Princes in the Tower, Bosworth.

groups.label: Tudors
groups.note: 1485–1603: Henry VIII, his children, and a nine-day queen.

groups.label: Stuarts
groups.note: 1603–1649: the crowns united, and one lost head.

groups.label: Commonwealth
groups.note: 1649–1660: no king at all. The Cromwells ruled as Lord Protectors.

groups.label: Stuarts restored
groups.note: 1660–1714: the Merry Monarch, a revolution, and the Union.

groups.label: Hanover
groups.note: 1714–1901: four Georges, a sailor, and Victoria.

groups.label: Saxe-Coburg and Windsor
groups.note: 1901–today: an abdication, the war, and seventy years of Elizabeth.

rhyme.title: The rhyme
rhyme.intro: The old schoolroom rhyme, brought up to date. Point at a line to see its monarchs on the timeline. It skips Lady Jane Grey and the Cromwells; so does history, mostly.

lines.text: One, two, three Neds, Richard two,
Harrys four, five, six… then who?
Edwards four, five, Dick the bad,
Harrys twain, and Ned the lad;
Then Charles the third: three hearty cheers!

items.name: William I
items.hook: The Conqueror. Won at Hastings in 1066, then wrote everything down in the Domesday Book in case anyone forgot.

items.name: William II
items.hook: “Rufus”, for his red face. Shot dead by an arrow while hunting in the New Forest. Accident? Nobody's quite sure.

items.name: Henry I
items.hook: Died, so the story goes, of a “surfeit of lampreys”: too many eels, against doctor's orders.

items.name: Stephen
items.hook: Strictly of the House of Blois. His reign was “the Anarchy”: nineteen years of civil war with his cousin Matilda.

items.name: Henry II
items.hook: First Plantagenet. His knights murdered Thomas Becket in Canterbury Cathedral after he reportedly asked to be rid of “this turbulent priest”.

items.name: Richard I
items.hook: The Lionheart. Spent about six months of his ten-year reign actually in England.

items.name: John
items.hook: Sealed Magna Carta in 1215, and reportedly lost the crown jewels in the Wash a year later.

items.name: Henry III
items.hook: King at nine, for 56 years. Rebuilt Westminster Abbey.

items.name: Edward I
items.hook: “Longshanks” for his height, and “Hammer of the Scots”. Ringed Wales with castles.

items.name: Edward II
items.hook: Lost Bannockburn to Robert the Bruce, then his throne to his own wife, Isabella, “the She-Wolf of France”.

items.name: Edward III
items.hook: Started the Hundred Years' War and founded the Order of the Garter.

items.name: Richard II
items.hook: King at ten, faced down the Peasants' Revolt at fourteen, deposed at thirty-two.

items.name: Henry IV
items.hook: Henry Bolingbroke: took the throne from his cousin Richard II and started the Lancaster line.

items.name: Henry V
items.hook: Agincourt, 1415. “Once more unto the breach”, in Shakespeare's version at least.

items.name: Henry VI
items.hook: King at nine months old. Lost France, his wits and, twice, the crown.

items.name: Edward IV
items.hook: First Yorkist king. Won the throne, lost it to Henry VI, then won it back.

items.name: Edward V
items.hook: One of the Princes in the Tower. Reigned about eleven weeks, never crowned, and vanished.

items.name: Richard III
items.hook: Lost at Bosworth in 1485; found under a Leicester car park in 2012.

items.name: Henry VII
items.hook: Won at Bosworth and married Elizabeth of York, uniting the roses: the Tudor rose is red and white.

items.name: Henry VIII
items.hook: Six wives: divorced, beheaded, died; divorced, beheaded, survived.

items.name: Edward VI
items.hook: Henry VIII's longed-for son: king at nine, dead at fifteen.

items.name: Lady Jane Grey
items.hook: The nine-day queen, proclaimed and then deposed by Mary I. Executed at sixteen or seventeen.

items.name: Mary I
items.hook: “Bloody Mary”: burned nearly three hundred Protestants, and lost Calais.

items.name: Elizabeth I
items.hook: The Virgin Queen: the Armada, Shakespeare, and the last of the Tudors.

items.name: James I
items.hook: Already James VI of Scotland: united the two crowns. The King James Bible, and the Gunpowder Plot.

items.name: Charles I
items.hook: The only English king to be executed: beheaded in 1649 after losing the Civil War.

items.name: Oliver Cromwell
items.hook: Lord Protector, not king: he turned the crown down. After the Restoration he was dug up and his head put on a spike.

items.name: Richard Cromwell
items.hook: “Tumbledown Dick”: inherited his father's job and lasted eight months.

items.name: Charles II
items.hook: The Merry Monarch: brought back theatre and fun after the Puritans. Once hid in an oak tree after losing at Worcester.

items.name: James II
items.hook: A Catholic king, deposed in the Glorious Revolution of 1688 by his own daughter and son-in-law.

items.name: William III
items.hook: William of Orange. Died after his horse tripped on a molehill; his enemies toasted “the little gentleman in the black velvet waistcoat”.

items.name: Mary II
items.hook: Reigned jointly with William, her husband and her cousin. Died of smallpox at 32.

items.name: Anne
items.hook: The last Stuart, and the first monarch of Great Britain, after the Act of Union with Scotland in 1707.

items.name: George I
items.hook: From Hanover, and spoke little English, so his ministers ran things: hello, first Prime Minister.

items.name: George II
items.hook: The last British king to lead an army into battle, at Dettingen in 1743.

items.name: George III
items.hook: Sixty years on the throne. Lost America, and later his mind.

items.name: George IV
items.hook: The Prince Regent: built Brighton Pavilion and spent like there was no tomorrow.

items.name: William IV
items.hook: The Sailor King, Victoria's uncle. No legitimate children, which is how we got Victoria.

items.name: Victoria
items.hook: 63 years and nine children, married into half of Europe's royal families: “the grandmother of Europe”.

items.name: Edward VII
items.hook: Waited nearly sixty years to be king, and gave his name to the Edwardian era.

items.name: George V
items.hook: Changed the family name to Windsor in 1917: Saxe-Coburg-Gotha sounded a bit too German mid-war.

items.name: Edward VIII
items.hook: Abdicated after 326 days to marry Wallis Simpson. Never crowned.

items.name: George VI
items.hook: Never meant to be king: the stammer of The King's Speech. Saw Britain through the war.

items.name: Elizabeth II
items.hook: Seventy years, the longest reign in British history: fifteen prime ministers, from Churchill to Truss.

items.name: Charles III
items.hook: The longest-waiting heir in British history: king at 73, in 2022.
